\# Updates bank account and payout method resources for Global Payouts

\## What’s new

\- Renames the \`enabled\_delivery\_options\` property to \[enabled\_delivery\_schemes\](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/money-management/payout-methods/object.md?api-version=2026-08-26.preview#v2\_payout\_method\_object-bank\_account-enabled\_delivery\_schemes) on the \[bank\_account\](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/money-management/payout-methods/object.md?api-version=2026-08-26.preview#v2\_payout\_method\_object-bank\_account) hash of the \[v2 Payout Method\](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/money-management/payout-methods.md?api-version=2026-08-26.preview) object. The new name better reflects that the property represents delivery schemes rather than generic options.
\- Adds the \[restricted\](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/vault/us-bank-accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-08-26.preview#v2\_us\_bank\_account\_object-restricted) property to \[US Bank Account\](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/vault/us-bank-accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-08-26.preview) and \[GB Bank Account\](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/vault/gb-bank-accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-08-26.preview) vault resources. This Boolean property indicates whether a user can use a correctly configured bank account for money movement. Without this field, users might infer blocked transactions as invalid configuration.

\## Why is this a breaking change?

Integrations that reference the \`enabled\_delivery\_options\` property of the v2 Payout Methods object’s \`bank\_account\` hash won’t receive expected data and might receive errors if they don’t handle the renamed property in their integration.

\## Impact

If your integration reads the \`enabled\_delivery\_options\` property from v2 Payout Method Bank Account objects, you must update your code to use \`enabled\_delivery\_schemes\` instead.

You can also now inspect the \`restricted\` property on vault bank accounts to determine whether a bank account can receive payouts on Stripe. This new functionality isn’t breaking and requires no change if you choose not to use it.

\## Upgrade

\#### REST API

1\. \[View your current API version\](https://docs.stripe.com/workbench/guides.md#view-api-versions) in Workbench.
2\. If you use an SDK, upgrade to the corresponding SDK version for this API version.
 \- If you don’t use an SDK, update your \[API requests\](https://docs.stripe.com/api-versions.md#how-versions-are-specified-in-requests) to include \`Stripe-Version: 2026-08-26.preview\`
3\. Upgrade the API version used for \[webhook endpoints\](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).
4\. \[Test your integration\](https://docs.stripe.com/testing.md) against the new version.
5\. If you use Connect, \[test your Connect integration\](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing.md).

Learn more about \[Stripe API upgrades\](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md).
